{{DISPLAYTITLE:tawaki}}
'''tawaki''' is Fiordland's package manager. It looks up a name in the Arch repos, on Flathub and in the AUR at the same time, and installs from the cleanest source. Source code: [https://github.com/3cfl/tawaki github.com/3cfl/tawaki].

== Commands ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Command !! Short !! What it does
|-
| <code>tawaki install firefox</code> || <code>i</code> || Install an app
|-
| <code>tawaki remove firefox</code> || <code>r</code>, <code>rm</code> || Remove an app, wherever it came from
|-
| <code>tawaki update</code> || <code>u</code>, <code>up</code> || Update everything: system, Flatpaks and AUR
|-
| <code>tawaki search obs</code> || <code>s</code> || Search all sources
|-
| <code>tawaki list</code> || <code>ls</code> || List what you installed with tawaki
|-
| <code>tawaki install foo --from aur</code> || || Force a source (<code>pacman</code>, <code>flatpak</code>, <code>aur</code>)
|}

The shell also has two shortcuts: <code>i</code> for <code>tawaki install</code> and <code>up</code> for <code>tawaki update</code>.

If you type a command that is not installed, the terminal tells you which package has it, for example <code>tawaki install btop</code>.

== Which source wins ==
By default: Arch repos first, then Flathub, then the AUR. If the Flathub version would need a large runtime you do not have yet, tawaki picks a prebuilt repo or AUR package instead and tells you how much download it saved.

Change the order in <code>~/.config/tawaki/config.toml</code>:
<pre>
priority = ["pacman", "flatpak", "aur"]
aur_helper = "auto"
flatpak_scope = "user"
flatpak_remote = "flathub"
prefer_light = true
</pre>

== About the AUR ==
The AUR is made of user-submitted build scripts. They are not reviewed by Arch or Fiordland. Prefer repo and Flathub packages, and only install AUR packages you trust.
